name: Ron Hardy
hook: Never released a record under his own name, but the DJ whose Music Box sets and tape edits broke half of Chicago house before it was ever pressed.
blurb: Hardy DJed at Chicago's Music Box from 1982 to 1986, using two turntables, a mixer and a reel-to-reel tape deck to edit and extend records live. Producers like Marshall Jefferson and Larry Heard brought him early tapes of their new tracks to test on his dancefloor before anyone else heard them. He never released music under his own name in his lifetime, so his influence survives mostly through secondhand accounts, bootleg reissues of his tape edits, and the records other producers made in direct response to what worked at the Music Box. That missing paper trail tells you something: some of the most important figures on this map, King Tubby included, shaped recorded music mainly through a room rather than through records with their names on.
signatureTracksNote: Never released a record under his own name. What he played at the Music Box is why he is here.
